limitations: Initial fuzz campaigns used Go default minimization and did not snapshot the interesting-input cache. Final campaigns explicitly use one-second minimization and snapshot cached corpus before and after.
The native worker sample has unresolved Go symbols and no retained matching worker binary; it does not establish a production CPU bottleneck.
Single 30-second sample per benchmark workload and stage; no statistical performance trend claimed.
The record labels environment-final refer to the subsequently rejected projection-reuse experiment, not package completion.
Stdlib critical-variable replay is not native Windows execution.
Raw source snapshots, profiles and matching binaries remain local and ignored.

Native Windows/Linux execution is unavailable here. Windows exit-259 held-handle tests are compiled, not claimed as executed. Consumer Blink changes are workspace validation, not published dependency adoption.
